answers.text: Give it three lines back - drop-off time, pallet count, damage noted - always in that order and clearly labelled.
List each call needing follow-up as its own line with time, customer, topic and outcome, then count the lines for the total. If a customer called twice, list both but note it.
The finish time is wrong - 8am plus about six hours lands early afternoon the same day, not the 23rd as the note says.
96 to 118 invoices comes out closer to 23%, not the 20% stated in the note.
Output 2, since it shows the 940 tickets and 827 closed that the 88% comes from.
Email 2, since it backs up the ask with real order volumes. Email 1's 'better rate' claim isn't checkable as it stands, though it isn't necessarily wrong.
The hourly rates and retainer cap are sensitive enough that I'd hold those back, and the non-disclosure clause naming both sides makes me cautious with the rest too.
Before the reconciliation summary goes out at month end, I check the totals against the warehouse system count.
Step 1, reading the invoice, seems like the one most worth watching since a bad extraction there would carry through.
